children: What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after AI linked stocks continued to pull back as Anthropic slid nearly 14% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

By midday, Nvidia dropped more than 7%—extending a 33% November decline—while Advanced Micro Devices fell 11%, Micron Technology lost 12%, SanDisk shed 14%, and CoreWeave tumbled almost 11%, CNBC reported. The Nasdaq Composite slid 3.6%, erasing its 2026 gains. Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported.

Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth. Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.

When borrowing costs climb and export controls tighten, investors stop treating the AI supply chain as a uniform growth trade. Until December's rate decision and next year's data-center budgets clarify spending returns, model makers, chipmakers, memory suppliers, and cloud operators remain vulnerable to shared valuation compression.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Hardware & infrastructure company ChronoScale Holdings fell 6.8%.
Hardware & infrastructure company IQM Quantum Computers fell 7.9%.
Hardware & infrastructure company SharonAI Holdings fell 19.4%.
Hardware & infrastructure company IREN fell 16.3%.

children: Zooming in on SharonAI Holdings

SharonAI Holdings’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 99 moves greater than 5% over the last year. But moves this big are rare even for SharonAI Holdings and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 3 days ago when the stock gained 9% on the news that the company reported third-quarter revenue rose 1,859% year on year and said it expected $400 million to $450 million in annualized run rate revenue (ARR) from January 2027.

According to the company's earnings release, SharonAI Holdings posted revenue of $9.9 million for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 414% from the second quarter of 2026, alongside a net loss of $43.8 million compared with a net loss of $1.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. The release also showed that approximately 30 megawatts (MW) of its 129 MW of contracted capacity is expected to be billing from January 2027, and detailed an approximately $1.0 billion, five-year take-or-pay contract with a global services company, a $170 million, four-year take-or-pay contract with a U.S.-based AI inference platform and data center energization for approximately 8,000 NVIDIA B300 and 4,000 NVIDIA GB300 clusters.

In addition, the company's earnings press release highlighted a $1.32 billion, five-year take-or-pay contract with a global AI lab and the delivery and acceptance of an approximately 1,000 NVIDIA B300 GPU cluster by a global technology company.
SharonAI Holdings is down 47.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $16.70 per share, it is trading 88% below its 52-week high of $139 from December 2025.
